text:
kevin: heads up — seeing a spike of transient OOMs on the cont-batch path for gptx-4g when batch size grows from 128 -> 192. repro profile attached, looks like allocator burst + kv-cache reclamation thrash.

mira: thanks for flagging. is this specific to the slab allocator or also on native cudaMalloc path?

kevin: repro on both, but behavior differs. with cudaMalloc we get long tail latency while the custom slab shows fragmentation leading to failed allocations at ~1.6GB free.

sam: can you paste the profiler snippet? curious about per-seq workspace spikes vs total resident.

kevin: pasted below — filtered to interesting bits. note the per-request workspace delta ~12KB/seq growing with padding.

```
# profile excerpt
time, cuda_alloc_calls, allocated_bytes, resident_bytes
00:00:01, 42, 120_000_000, 2_450_000_000
00:00:02, 61, 180_000_000, 2_470_000_000
00:00:03, 78, 240_000_000, 1_900_000_000  # OOM shortly after
```

kevin: looks like batch growth increases padding waste nonlinearly; per-seq overhead isn't being charged to the batch reservation so allocator overcommits.

jules: that matches a recent change in accounting where we stopped including ephemeral KV scratch in the batch reservation to reduce reservation pressure. seems we introduced double-free complexity in the free list compaction too.

mira: big picture: two levers — tighten reservation to include ephemeral buffers (prefix/kvcache temp), or improve reuse so padding doesn't trigger new allocations. which is lower risk?

sam: reuse wins for perf but is a bit invasive. short-term patch: add a soft-reserve margin (10%) to the batch reservation and trigger proactive KV eviction when batch_count > 150. reduces thrash.

kevin: I ran a smoke with +10% soft-reserve and aggressive kv-evict on growth threshold — OOMs disappeared in 2000 QPS test. p99 latency +8ms but stable.

mira: nice. can we make the reserve adaptive instead of fixed +10%? maybe measure live padding saturation and set reserve = max(soft, percentile(padding*seq_count)).

sam: yep — heuristic: reserve = max( base_reserve, ceil( p95_padding_per_seq * expected_batch_seqs ) ). implemented locally like:

```
def compute_reserve(base, p95_padding, batch_seqs):
    return max(base, math.ceil(p95_padding * batch_seqs))
```

sam: also added an opportunistic buffer pool for ephemeral KV temps keyed by (seq_len_bucket, dtype). reuse rate went from 22%->72% in profiler.

jules: did the pool reduce fragmentation? any measurement of max resident after changes?

kevin: yes, resident peak dropped ~430MB on the run with the pool + adaptive reserve. no OOMs. patch diff: short excerpt below.

```
# allocator config
allocator:
  strategy: slab
  reserve_margin_pct: auto   # computes from p95 padding
  temp_pool:
    enabled: true
    buckets: [32,64,128,256,512]
```

mira: sounds promising. two questions: 1) KV eviction policy — are we using async background eviction or inline blocking evict? 2) any perf regression for small batches (<32)?

sam: eviction is async but we now have a fast-path inline attempt: try_reclaim_sync() returns quickly if it finds contiguous blocks; otherwise enqueue background eviction. small batches unaffected in my test harness.

kevin: one oddity: on machines with high fragmentation (older drivers) the slab free list compaction is expensive and causes p95 CPU jitter. we should gate compaction frequency by allocation failure rate, not time.

jules: agree. also we should add a telemetry histogram for "per_seq_padding_bytes" and emit p50/p95 along with batch-size metrics. that will make adaptive reserve safer.

mira: next steps:
- ship temporary +10% soft-reserve + kv-evict threshold as rollback-safe toggle (sam)
- prototype adaptive reserve + temp pool as feature branch (sam + kevin)
- add telemetry for per_seq_padding_bytes and slab_frag_pct (jules)
- limit compaction frequency by alloc_fail_rate in allocator (kevin)

kevin: I'll open a PR for the soft-reserve + kv-evict today, include smoke results and perf numbers. attaching run summary: p50 latency same, p95 stable, p99 reduced spikes, resident -430MB.

infra-bot: deploy queued: deploy/cont-batch-alpha -> infra-staging (by kevin)

mira: thanks — once PR is up I'll review. ideally we keep the soft-reserve behind a feature flag so we can A/B with live traffic. :thumbsup:

sam: FYI: long-term we should also look at kernel selection impacts on mem churn — some kernels allocate temporaries internally that we don't account for. might need a kernel-level declared_temp_bytes API so the allocator can plan ahead.

kevin: good note — added to the backlog. for now let's get the pool+adaptive reserve validated in staging.

jules: great thread. saved my notes to the perf board.

kevin: thanks all, will post PR link and smoke logs once CI finishes.
